title: Coherent State
intro: A harmonic well (the rings are equipotentials) pulls the packet back and forth with period T = 2π/ω. Released from rest, a Gaussian generally breathes as it swings: its width oscillates between σ and 1/(2ωσ) twice per period. Exactly one width, σ₀ = 1/√(2ω), keeps its shape at all times: the coherent state, the quantum state that moves most like a classical particle. The detector clicks at t = 9T/8, as the packet passes the target.
goal: Choose the packet's width σ. The packet swings in the well, and the detector clicks by itself at t ≈ 14.1, when the packet passes the target.

physics.point: In a harmonic well one width, σ₀ = 1/√(2ω), swings back and forth without changing shape. This coherent state is the most classical motion quantum mechanics allows.

idea: The potential rises as the square of the distance from the centre, like a ball on a spring. A classical ball released at x = 26 swings to x = 14 and back with period T = 2π/ω, whatever the amplitude. The centre of the packet does exactly the same.

Its width behaves differently. A narrow packet contains a wide spread of momenta, so it spreads out, and the well then squeezes it back. A wide packet contains few momenta, and the well squeezes it first. Either way the width oscillates twice per period: the packet breathes.

One width balances the two: σ₀ = 1/√(2ω), the width of the well's ground state. That packet keeps its shape and its minimum uncertainty, Δx·Δk = ½, at every moment. It is called a coherent state, and it is the closest a quantum particle gets to a point mass on a spring.
The detector clicks at t = 9T/8, one eighth of a period after a full swing. A breathing packet is then wider than σ₀, so less of it falls in the target.
maths: With ω = 0.5 the period is T = 2π/ω ≈ 12.57. The centre follows x(t) = 20 + 6 cos ωt, which at t = 9T/8 (ωt = 9π/4) is 20 + 6/√2 ≈ 24.24, the centre of the target.

try: Set σ = 1 and watch: the blob swings without changing size, and P_T at the click is about 65%.

Set σ = 0.4. A quarter period later the packet has grown to 2.5, and by half a period it is narrow again. Then try σ = 2.5. At the click both packets have the same width and both give P_T ≈ 30%, because 1/(2ωσ) turns 0.4 into 2.5 and back.
